verdict_reason: The load-bearing §4.2 strip holds end-to-end: the SQL read never selects form_token/objection_detail/fraud_signals columns, deletes the raw referee IP/UA paths via jsonb #- under jsonb_typeof guards, and the integration suite (498 passed, run by the lead at a7e8cee5) seeds a row carrying EVERY internal marker and asserts absence in both unescaped AND escaped wire forms plus raw values, with live negative controls. findings.title: §4.2 belt-and-braces guard checks escaped wire forms for referee_ip/UA only — form_token/payload_ref escaped forms are unchecked despite the 'both forms are checked' doc claim
findings.evidence: let markers = [ "\"form_token\"", "\"payload_ref\"", "\"referee_ip\"", "\"referee_user_agent\"", "\\\"referee_ip\\\"", "\\\"referee_user_agent\\\"", ] / doc: 'both forms are checked so the guard can't be beaten by the escaping (Perkins-style lens finding, rc4-1 self-review #1)'
findings.detail: Keys inside the result JSON-string field ship backslash-escaped on the wire; the escaped markers cover only referee_ip/referee_user_agent. A corrupt/spoofed stored result containing form_token or payload_ref keys at any path would pass the guard clean. The negative-control test feeds those two markers only in the unescaped top-level form the encoder never emits.
findings.recommended_fix: Add "\\\"form_token\\\"" and "\\\"payload_ref\\\"" to the markers list and extend verify_payload_guard_detects_internal_markers_test with the escaped result-string forms.

findings.title: Unknown outcome value serialises as terminal "unreachable" while hooks (status-derived) can still say can_record_manual: true — a fabricated state on the wire
findings.evidence: outcome: case row.outcome { "" -> None; s -> Some(shared_reference_call.outcome_from_string(s)) } / shared:215 '_ -> OutcomeUnreachable' / pinned by 'unknown_outcome_never_falls_back_to_success_test'
findings.detail: During an enum expand-then-contract window, an old server reading a new outcome value renders 'unreachable' on a row whose hooks say recordable — the exact hooks-vs-wire divergence the PR's self-review #3 claims to prevent (status falls back inertly to failed; outcome does not). Impossible with today's 16-value enum, real in the expand window.
findings.recommended_fix: Map unrecognised outcome strings to None (absent) in encode_reference_call instead of round-tripping OutcomeUnreachable, so the wire never asserts an unreachable state the row did not reach.

findings.title: verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields is dead code in production — test-only; doc comment overstates a runtime re-verification
findings.evidence: pub fn verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields(payload: String) -> Bool { / grep: only test call sites; handle_get_detail + encode_reference_call never invoke it
findings.detail: The doc says 'this re-verifies the serialized payload can never carry the internal-only markers' — reads as a runtime backstop, but the guard is invoked only by tests. The SQL strip + encoder whitelist remain the real boundary (correct and integration-pinned), so this is doc-accuracy, not a leak.
findings.recommended_fix: Either invoke the guard on the built body in handle_get_detail (fail/log loudly on False), or demote the doc claim to 'test-only assertion'.

findings.title: SQL ELSE branch passes string-typed intermediates verbatim — the 'cannot leak' comment is false for double-encoded corrupt rows
findings.evidence: 'when any level is not an object the form_session key path cannot exist, so passing the result through verbatim cannot leak the §4.2 keys.' / CASE ... jsonb_typeof(result->'fraud_signals') = 'object' ... THEN (result #- ...)::text ELSE result::text END
findings.detail: If a corrupt row stores fraud_signals/form_session as a JSON *string* containing escaped JSON, typeof='string' → ELSE → the escaped key text rides the wire. No current writer produces that shape (all server-built objects), so it is corrupt-row-only; the corrupt-row test seeds only a scalar ('42'::jsonb), leaving the string-intermediate shape untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the comment to state the object-writer invariant, and add a corrupt-row test seeding a string-intermediate fraud_signals containing the internal keys.

findings.title: next_attempt_at ships as timestamptz::text ("2026-08-01 09:00:00+00", session-TZ-dependent) while attempts[].at and fixtures use ISO-T — two datetime formats in one §8.1 entry
findings.evidence: COALESCE(next_attempt_at::text, '') AS next_attempt_at, / fixture: next_attempt_at: "2026-08-01T09:00:00Z" / attempts: [{\"at\":\"2026-08-01T08:00:00Z\"...}]
findings.detail: Verified at the test DB: timestamptz::text renders '2026-08-01 09:00:00+00'. Consistent with the house ::text convention (created_at elsewhere) and the client's format_timestamp_short handles both forms, so not a defect today — but RC4.2 must not assume a single format, and the offset shifts with session TZ.
findings.recommended_fix: Either document the ::text form in the §8.1 contract, or emit ISO-T (to_char AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') so next_attempt_at matches the attempt log.

findings.title: Shared attempt_decoder is strict (all 4 keys required) while sweep/result parsers are tolerant — one key-less entry silently empties the whole attempts array on the wire
findings.evidence: use at <- decode.field("at", decode.string) ... detail <- decode.field("detail", decode.string) / sweep: use at <- decode.optional_field("at", "", decode.string) x4 / parse_attempt_log: Error(_) -> []
findings.detail: The integration append API demonstrably accepts a 3-key entry (reference_checks_integration_test.gleam:284-286 appends {at,channel,outcome} with no detail). All current real writers emit 4 keys, so today's data is fine; a legacy/future 3-key entry would decode-fail the whole list and the panel would show an empty log.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the shared decoder with the sweep's tolerance (optional_field + '' defaults) so a partial entry degrades per-entry instead of wiping the whole log.

findings.title: ApplicationDetail envelope codec round-trips only the new-field defaults (reference_calls: [], attestation_on_file: False)
findings.detail: A populated reference_calls entry and attestation_on_file: true never traverse encode→decoder at the envelope level. The entry codec itself is round-trip tested (reference_call_test), but a broken envelope wiring (e.g. decode.list mis-use) would pass CI and break production decoding.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a third application_detail_codec round-trip carrying one populated ReferenceCallDetail plus attestation_on_file: True.

findings.title: Attempt-log writer/reader shape agreement is unpinned — the wire test asserts only the "attempts" key, not decoded content
findings.detail: If the sweep ever writes an entry the strict shared decoder rejects, parse_attempt_log degrades to [] and the panel silently shows an empty log; the key-presence assertion stays green either way. No test proves a sweep-built entry round-trips through attempt_decoder.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert a decoded attempt's content on the wire (e.g. "\"channel\": \"email\"") or unit-test a sweep-built outcome_entry through the shared attempt_decoder.

findings.title: No cross-tenant negative test for the new reference_calls/attestation read paths
findings.detail: All six new integration tests (and every existing detail test) use the owning landlord. The reads are gated by the pre-existing landlord-scoped outer query, so no leak is reachable — but nothing pins that a foreign landlord gets 404/no reference data for another landlord's application.
findings.recommended_fix: Seed landlord_b and assert handle_get_detail returns 404 (or empty reference_calls) when landlord_a requests landlord_b's application.
